messages.author: 4c03fb941a15202c
messages.subject: Own DEM in micro_era5
parts:
Hello,
I was able to use my own DEM with a resolution of 5m in the past.
Now after the update maybe. when I call dem = "my_dem" in micro_era5 it always downloads dem via elevatr.
Did anything change?

my code:
DEP <- c(0, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200)
dem <- raster(('F:/NICHE/NICHE/dem.tif'))
micro <- micro_era5(loc = lonlat,
dstart = dstart,
dfinish = dfinish,
dem = dem,
DEP = DEP,
runmoist = 0,
runshade = 0,
Usrhyt = 2,
dem.res = resolution,
spatial = folder)

Kind Regards,
André

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Own DEM in micro_era5
parts:
Dear André,

I think it's because I've switched it over to use terra rather than raster (after the rgdal retirement). You are reading your raster in with the raster package and so it isn't turning into an object of class 'SpatRaster' and the check in the micro_era5 function is    
 if(class(dem)[1] == "SpatRaster"){
      cat('using DEM provided to function call \n')
    }
So instead do:
dem <- terra::rast("F:/NICHE/NICHE/dem.tif")
All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Own DEM in micro_era5
parts:
It is a microclima issue I think, with the relevant microclima code below. Try running with cad.effects = FALSE and see if it works. If it does, you know it's to do with the 'if (costal) {' section. Otherwise it's from the 'eleveffects' function. 'demmeso' is the 'dem2' input of micro_era5 and defaults to use the dem you passed into the function as 'dem = '.

All the best,
Mike

  cat("Calculating meso-scale terrain effects \n")
  info <- .eleveffects(hourlydata, demmeso, lat, long, windthresh, emthresh, weather.elev, cad.effects)
  elev <- info$tout
  if (coastal) {
    m <- is_raster(dem)
    m[m == zmin] <- NA
    dem <- if_raster(m, dem)
    acoast <- coastalNCEP(dem, hourlydata, steps, use.raster, zmin, plot.progress, tidyr = FALSE)
    xi <- floor(dim(dem)[1] / 2)
    yi <- floor(dim(dem)[2] / 2)
    ce <- acoast[xi, yi, ]
    if (is.na(ce[1])) ce <- apply(acoast, 3, mean, na.rm = T)
    elev$tref <- ce - elev$tref + elev$telev
  }
